language.pt: bem como numa faixa de proteção de 500 metros
language.en: as well as in a protection strip of 500 metres
language.note: bem como = as well as: the ban covers the place itself and the strip around it too; it is never a contrast.

nudge: Land 'adjacentes a estabelecimentos hospitalares' carries the 500-metre strip, like schools and bathing beaches (questions 366 and 379). Settlements carry a narrower one, 250 metros (question 365), and the bank gives fruit crops no strip at all.

language.pt: bem como numa faixa de proteção de 500 metros
language.en: as well as in a protection strip of 500 metres
language.note: bem como = as well as: the ban covers the place itself and the strip around it too; it is never a contrast.

nudge: Land 'adjacentes a instalações militares ou de forças de segurança' carries the 500-metre strip, the same 500 metres question 396 asks for. Railway lines carry only 100 metros (question 382), and the bank gives vegetable crops no strip at all.

language.pt: bem como numa faixa de proteção
language.en: as well as in a protection strip
language.note: bem como = as well as: the ban covers the place itself and the strip around it too; it is never a contrast.

language.en: but only when there is traffic
language.note: mas só quando = but only when: a ban limited to the times traffic is passing.

nudge: National roads and railway lines are banned 'bem como numa faixa de proteção de 100 metros', whether or not traffic is passing. Questions 374 and 382 ask the same width for each alone, and 250 metres is the strip round settlements (question 365).
Settlements, 'os povoados', carry a 250-metre strip. The 500-metre strip belongs to places such as hospitals, schools and bathing beaches (questions 362 and 366), and no question sets one at 750.

language.pt: bem como numa faixa de proteção de 500 metros
language.en: as well as in a protection strip of 500 metres
language.note: bem como = as well as: the ban covers the place itself and the strip around it too; it is never a contrast.

nudge: 'Praias de banho' and land 'adjacentes a estabelecimentos de ensino' both carry the 500-metre strip (questions 376 and 379). National roads carry 100 metres (question 364) and aerodromes are banned ground in themselves (question 369), so neither road list is the 500-metre one.

language.pt: bem como em quaisquer terrenos que os circundem
language.en: as well as on any land surrounding them
language.note: bem como extends the ban from the places to the land around them; quaisquer = any, and os circundem = surround them, os standing for the places the options name.

nudge: Apiaries and dovecotes, 'apiários e pombais devidamente sinalizados', are banned with a 100-metre strip around them. A signposted livestock enclosure is banned ground in itself (question 371), and olive groves are banned only when signposted (question 401).

The 500-metre strip runs round 'Instalações turísticas, parques de campismo e desportivos'. Aerodromes, cemeteries and municipal roads are banned ground in themselves (question 369), and so are game refuges and signposted livestock enclosures (questions 407 and 371), but none of them is keyed with the 500-metre strip.

language.en: It is always prohibited
language.note: sempre = always: a ban with no condition.

nudge: Aerodromes, cemeteries and municipal roads are banned 'sempre', with no condition attached. Olive groves are banned only when signposted (question 401), and question 398 allows hunting among trees averaging over 80cm, so tall plantations are no absolute ban.

language.pt: A 300 metros das casas de habitação
language.en: At 300 metres from dwelling houses
language.note: a 300 metros de = at a distance of 300 metres from: the hunter stands that far away, not anywhere within it.

nudge: Livestock enclosures, 'aparcamentos de gado', are banned ground (question 371 adds 'devidamente sinalizado'). At 300 metres a hunter is outside the 250-metre strip round a dwelling (question 402), and at 250 metres outside the 100-metre strip of a national road (question 364).

language.pt: a menos de 250 metros dos animais
language.en: less than 250 metres from the animals
language.note: a menos de = at less than, within: the ban would reach only up to 250 metres from the animals.

nudge: In a signposted livestock enclosure 'É proibido caçar' across the whole enclosure, with no distance from the animals involved. Fighting cattle and 250 metres do not come into it, and question 370 bans hunting 'Nos aparcamentos de gado' just as plainly.

language.pt: sem consentimento de quem de direito
language.en: without the consent of the person entitled
language.note: sem = without: the ban holds only while the consent of the person entitled is missing, so with it hunting is allowed.

language.pt: há um deles que carece obrigatoriamente de sinalização
language.en: there is one of them that necessarily requires signposting
language.note: há um deles que = there is one of them that: the stem asks for the single exception. carecer de = to need, require.

nudge: The consent rule needs signs only in 'Zonas de caça': question 380 puts it as 'só é eficaz e depende de sinalização' there. Yards and gardens 'anexos a casas de habitação' are consent ground with no sign required.

language.en: provided that it has no olives
language.note: desde que = provided that, with the present subjunctive tenha: a condition attached to the yes.

nudge: An olive grove is closed to hunting only when it carries the no-hunting sign (questions 393 and 401), and this is that sign (question 375), so 'Não'. Whether the trees bear olives makes no difference.

language.pt: bem como numa faixa de proteção de
language.en: as well as in a protection strip of
language.note: bem como = as well as: the ban covers the place itself and the strip around it too; it is never a contrast.

nudge: A national road is banned 'bem como numa faixa de proteção de' 100 metros. The same 100 metres covers railway lines (questions 364 and 382), and 250 metres is the strip round settlements (question 365).

The red-over-white sign is the sinal de proibição de caçar: it marks 'Proibição de caçar'. It does not mark a tourist hunting zone or a livestock enclosure, and questions 373, 394 and 397 each key a ban on hunting where it stands.

language.en: From what distance
language.note: a partir de = from … onwards: the distance beyond which hunting is allowed, so the answer is the outer edge of the banned strip.

nudge: Hunting is allowed from 500 metros of a school, since land 'adjacentes a estabelecimentos de ensino' carries the 500-metre strip (question 366). At 150 or 200 metres a hunter is still inside it.

language.pt: bem como numa faixa de 250 metros em redor
language.en: as well as in a strip of 250 metres around them
language.note: bem como extends the ban to the strip; em redor = around the burnt area.

language.en: Only while the fire lasts
language.note: só = only, enquanto = while: a ban that would end when the fire goes out.

nudge: Burnt areas, with their 250-metre strip, stay closed 'Enquanto dura o incêndio e durante os 30 dias seguintes'. The ban outlasts the fire, so 'Só enquanto' is too short, and 10 days is the wrong count.
In walked-up hunting on unmanaged ground a line may hold at most '5 caçadores'. The number decides; 2 and 10 are the distractors.

language.pt: bem como numa faixa de proteção de
language.en: as well as in a protection strip of
language.note: bem como = as well as: the ban covers the place itself and the strip around it too; it is never a contrast.

nudge: Bathing beaches carry the 500-metre strip, like schools and hospitals (questions 362 and 366). 100 metres belongs to national roads and railway lines (question 364).

language.pt: só é eficaz e depende de sinalização
language.en: is only effective, and depends on signposting
language.note: só = only; eficaz = in force, effective: the stem asks for the one case where the ban works only once signs are up.

language.pt: sem consentimento de quem de direito
language.en: without the consent of the person entitled
language.note: sem = without: the ban holds only while the consent of the person entitled is missing, so with it hunting is allowed.

nudge: As question 372 keys, the case where the consent rule 'só é eficaz e depende de sinalização' is 'Nas zonas de caça'. Yards 'anexos a casas de habitação' are the near miss: question 372 lists them as consent ground that needs no sign.

language.en: more than 100 metres from
language.note: a mais de = at more than, beyond: every option places the hunter outside a 100-metre line, and the question is whose strip that clears.

nudge: Railway lines carry a 100-metre strip (question 382), so 'a mais de 100 metros', beyond it, hunting is allowed. Bathing beaches carry 500 metres (question 379), so 100 metres is still inside their strip, and the 100-metre rule is not given for airports.

language.pt: bem como numa faixa de proteção de
language.en: as well as in a protection strip of
language.note: bem como = as well as: the ban covers the place itself and the strip around it too; it is never a contrast.

nudge: A railway line is banned 'bem como numa faixa de proteção de' 100 metros, the same width as a national road (questions 364 and 374). 150 and 200 metres are distractors.

The 100-metre strip along railway lines is a flat ban: the hunter 'Nunca pode caçar' there. Consent of the person entitled lifts the ban round a dwelling's yard (question 402), not this one, and going without a firearm changes nothing.

language.en: at 250 metres from
language.note: a 250 metros de = at a distance of 250 metres from: the hunter stands that far away.

nudge: At 250 metres a hunter is beyond the 100-metre strip of a railway line (question 382), so it is allowed. Bathing beaches carry 500 metres (question 379), so 250 metres from one is still inside the strip.

language.en: lower than 1,2 g/l
language.note: inferior a = below, lower than a figure; not 'inferior' in quality.

nudge: Hunting 'em zonas de caça às quais não se tenha legalmente acesso' is a crime. A blood alcohol level 'inferior a 1,2 g/l' is no crime (question 403), and hunting wild boar on snow is allowed (question 27).

'Utilizar auxiliares fora das condições estabelecidas', using assistants outside the set rules, is a hunting crime, and question 410 is the same question. Lure calls are allowed for ducks (question 28), and 50 metres from a tarred municipal road is not keyed as a crime.

Only species 'que constem do calendário venatório publicado anualmente' may be hunted. Being classed as game is not enough, and damage to farming does not by itself make a species huntable (question 53 is the same question).
Buckshot, zagalotes, 'É proibida na caça', with no exception for fox drives or boar montarias in any kind of zone. Question 389 says the same: such cartridges 'Não podem ser utilizados na caça'.

language.en: commonly called
language.note: vulgarmente = commonly, in everyday speech; a false friend, not 'vulgarly'. designados por = called.

nudge: Shot over 4,5 mm, the zagalotes, 'Não podem ser utilizados na caça' at all, as question 388 also keys. Neither fox hunting nor stalking red deer is an exception.

language.en: The use and the possession
language.note: detenção = possession, keeping on one's person; a false friend, not 'detention'. The ban covers carrying the cartridges, not only firing them.

nudge: For resident small game the ban falls on 'cartuchos carregados com bala', slug cartridges, both using and carrying them. Question 392 is the mirror, banning shot for big game, and hunting dogs are not banned here.

language.pt: que comportem mais de três munições
language.en: that hold more than three rounds
language.note: comportar = to hold, take (of a magazine), not 'behave'; mais de três = more than three, so four or more.

nudge: Semi-automatic guns 'que comportem mais de três munições' are banned outright: 'É proibida'. The two 'permitida' options invent exceptions for big game and thrushes that the keyed ban does not have.

language.en: The use and the possession
language.note: detenção = possession, keeping on one's person; a false friend, not 'detention'. The ban covers carrying the cartridges, not only firing them.

nudge: For big game the ban falls on 'cartuchos carregados com chumbos', shot cartridges, both using and carrying them. Question 390 is the mirror, banning slugs for resident small game, and the keyed ban is on the cartridges, not on shotguns.
Olive groves are closed only 'Se estiverem sinalizados com o sinal de proibição de caçar'. 'Sempre' and 'Nunca' both ignore that condition, and question 401 asks the same.

language.en: with the consent
language.note: mediante = by means of, upon: the two options make hunting depend on someone's consent.

nudge: The no-hunting sign of question 375 closes the ground: 'Não se pode caçar', and this question keys that flat ban over both consent options. Question 397 words what the same sign forbids as 'Caçar sem consentimento de quem de direito'; the junta de freguesia comes into neither.

language.en: does not constitute a hunting crime
language.note: não constitui = does not constitute: the stem asks for the one act that is not a crime, so two of the options are crimes.

nudge: A blood alcohol level 'inferior a 1,2 g/l', below the line, is no hunting crime (questions 403 and 405). Hunting non-game species is a crime (question 406), and so is hunting in no-hunting areas (question 400 keys it for areas under the right to no hunting).

language.en: From what distance
language.note: a partir de = from … onwards: the distance beyond which hunting is allowed, so the answer is the outer edge of the banned strip.

nudge: Hunting is allowed from 500 metros of a military installation, the strip of question 363. At 200 or 250 metres a hunter is still inside it.

language.en: it is not permitted
language.note: não é permitido = is not permitted: the stem asks for the one thing the sign forbids.

nudge: The no-hunting sign of question 375 forbids hunting, which this question words as 'Caçar sem consentimento de quem de direito' and question 394 as a flat 'Não se pode caçar'. Training dogs and the wider 'atividades de caráter cinegético' are not what the keyed answer forbids.

language.en: provided that the hunter is a member
language.note: desde que = provided that, with the present subjunctive seja: a condition attached to the permission.

language.en: less than 100 metres from
language.note: a menos de = at less than, within 100 metres.

nudge: Hunting is allowed in a pine wood whose trees average 'superior a 80cm', and question 399 allows it at 1 metre too. Club membership does not open a game refuge, and 'a menos de 100 metros' of a national road is inside its strip (question 364).

language.en: It is always prohibited to hunt
language.note: sempre = always: a ban with no condition.

language.pt: desde que o diâmetro do tronco seja inferior a 5 cm
language.en: provided that the diameter of the trunk is less than 5 cm
language.note: desde que = provided that, with the present subjunctive seja: here it attaches a condition to the ban; inferior a = below.

nudge: At an average of 1 metre the trees are above the 80cm of question 398, so 'É permitido caçar'. The ban is not 'sempre', and trunk diameter is no test anywhere in the bank.

language.en: without carrying
language.note: sem trazer consigo = without having it on one's person: the hunter holds the certificate but has left it behind.

nudge: Hunting 'em áreas de direito à não caça' is a hunting crime. Lacking a licence or not carrying the carta is not keyed as a crime, while question 409 makes hunting 'sem estar habilitado com carta de caçador', with no carta at all, one.

language.en: it is always prohibited
language.note: sempre = always: a ban with no condition.

nudge: Olive groves are closed 'Só quando sinalizados com o sinal de proibição de caçar', as question 393 also keys. 'Sim, é sempre proibido' and a flat 'Não' both drop that condition.

language.pt: bem como numa faixa envolvente de 250 metros
language.en: as well as in a surrounding strip of 250 metres
language.note: bem como = as well as: the same rule covers the yard and the 250-metre strip round it; envolvente = surrounding.

nudge: A yard and its 250-metre strip are closed to hunting only 'sem consentimento de quem de direito', so with that consent hunting is allowed. Neither 'Sempre proibido' nor 'Sempre permitido' fits, and question 408 applies the same rule at 200 metres.

language.en: does not constitute a hunting crime
language.note: não constitui = does not constitute: the stem asks for the one act that is not a crime, so two of the options are crimes.

language.en: higher than 1,2g/l
language.note: superior a = above, higher than a figure; not 'superior' in quality. With inferior a (below) and igual a (equal to), the options sit above, below and on the same figure.

nudge: Only 'inferior a 1,2g/l', below the line, is no crime. 'superior a' and 'igual a 1,2g/l' are both crimes, so the line itself already counts.

language.pt: bem como numa faixa de proteção de
language.en: as well as in a protection strip of
language.note: bem como = as well as: the ban covers the place itself and the strip around it too; it is never a contrast.

nudge: As in question 374, a national road is banned 'bem como numa faixa de proteção de' 100 metros. 150 and 200 metres are distractors.

language.en: does not constitute a hunting crime
language.note: não constitui = does not constitute: the stem asks for the one act that is not a crime, so two of the options are crimes.

nudge: A blood alcohol level 'inferior a 1,2g/l' is no crime (question 403). Keeping or using a ferret 'sem autorização' and using assistants outside the set conditions (question 386) are both hunting crimes.
Hunting a non-game species is a 'Crime de caça', not merely an administrative offence. Question 395 counts it among the crimes too.

language.pt: só se torna eficaz desde que sinalizados
language.en: only becomes effective provided that they are signposted
language.note: só = only; se torna eficaz = takes effect; desde que = provided that: the ban works only once the ground is signposted.

nudge: Game refuges are banned only once signposted: the ban 'só se torna eficaz desde que sinalizados'. Burnt land is closed for the fire and 30 days after with no sign needed (question 377), and tourist installations and campsites carry a 500-metre strip (question 368).

language.en: may the act of hunting be carried out
language.note: praticar-se = be carried out, passive se: the stem asks whether hunting is allowed there at all.

language.en: Yes, but only
language.note: mas só = but only: a yes limited to one condition; two options share it, so read what follows.

nudge: 200 metres is inside the 250-metre strip round a dwelling, where hunting is banned 'sem consentimento de quem de direito' (question 402). So it is allowed 'mas só com autorização de quem de direito', not freely and not limited to hunting from a hide.

Hunting 'sem estar habilitado com carta de caçador', without holding a carta at all, is a hunting crime. An identity card is not the test, and 200 metres from a signposted dovecote is outside its 100-metre strip (question 367).

As in question 386, 'Utilizar auxiliares fora das condições estabelecidas' is a hunting crime. Lure calls are allowed for ducks (question 28), and 50 metres from a tarred municipal road is not keyed as a crime.

'Abandonar os animais que auxiliam e acompanham o caçador', abandoning the hunter's working animals, is a hunting crime. A blood alcohol level of 1,0 g/l is below the 1,2 line (question 403), and the duck hide case is not keyed as a crime.

language.en: not identified by ministerial order
language.note: The não belongs to identificadas: the stem is about species and subspecies that the order does not list.

language.en: provided that the production
language.note: desde que = provided that, with the present subjunctive (seja, se destine): a condition attached to the permission.

nudge: Captive breeding of game species 'não identificadas em portaria' is 'Proibida', whatever the production is for. Neither food nor releases on training grounds makes it lawful, despite the 'desde que' options.
